decisive_items: intensely FDG-avid, partially calcified 4.1 × 2.3 × 2.8 cm expansile lesion within the right hyoid bone
interval growth of the hyoid bone lesion, suggesting a distinct pathology
A multidisciplinary sarcoma tumor board concluded that the hyoid lesion most likely represented a synchronous primary bone tumor (e.g., plasmacytoma, chondrosarcoma, or osteosarcoma)
response.rationale: The lung mass responded to Ewing-directed chemotherapy, whereas the hyoid lesion progressed, indicating a separate chemotherapy-resistant process. Among the listed bone tumors, a partially calcified expansile hyoid lesion is most consistent with chondrosarcoma; plasmacytoma is typically lytic and osteosarcoma is less supported.

rejected.why: The lung lesion was Ewing/PNET and responded to VCD/IE, but the hyoid lesion grew during treatment, so it is a distinct pathology rather than Ewing sarcoma.
Plasmacytoma would be an unusual cause of a partially calcified expansile hyoid lesion and is typically lytic, making it less likely than chondrosarcoma.
Osteosarcoma can produce calcification, but the imaging description and clinical context better fit chondrosarcoma; osteosarcoma is less likely in the hyoid without more aggressive features.
